sentences.text:
The Petitioner has filed this Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying for the following substantive reliefs :
"(b) That this Hon'ble Court may kindly be issued appropriate Writ and thereby be pleased to declare that the action of Respondents is illegal and bad-in-law in respect of acquisition of the said property of the Petitioner and acquisition is initiated without following any procedure under the law nor paid proper compensation for the said acquisition and in violation of their right to property under Art. 300A of the Constitution of India in view of the settled law and in consequences therefore, be pleased to direct the Respondents to award compensation as against the said property which is likely to be acquired for the National Highway no.60(Old No.50)
including all statutory benefits, interest, solatium etc till its realization under the prevailing law i.e. the said Act, 2013 as per today's market prevailing with interest and all benefits.
(c) That this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to direct the Respondent no.1 to 5 to follow the process of acquisition in respect of the said land of the Petitioner and thereby fresh process of acquisition be initiated for land of the Petitioner which they are in process of acquiring more than the land for which compensation is awarded and thereby award be passed under the prevailing law and compensation, solatium Kiran Vasantrao Manjare vs The Collector Pune And Ors on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139729787/
2 and other benefits be granted with interest to the Petitioner.

sentences.text:
(d) That this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to direct the Respondents to do measurement of the said property of the Petitioner to determine the exact areas which is acquired and which they proposed to acquire for the said National Highway No.60 (Old No.50) and thereby be directed to pay compensation for the land which is not paid and further the Respondents be directed to initiate fresh acquisition process in respect to the said area which they propose to acquire and compensation be awarded under the prevailing law.
(e) This Hon'ble Court may be pleased to direct the Respondents No.2 to 4 to repay the amount of Rs.1,16,44,830/- for 7 R (reducing the amount of Rs.40,04,404/-
which is paid to the Petitioner) which is due and payable to the Petitioner and as per the award dated 8/11/2017 and the said amount be paid alongwith interest."

04 October, 2024.
Priya Soparkar 39 wp 4742-22-c.doc 4.

The Petitioner has contended that the land in question, namely, Gut No.1205 of village Chakan,
Taluka Khed, District Pune falling within the limits of Chakan Municipal Council ad-measuring total area of 00 H.65 Acres is owned by the Petitioner.

It is the Petitioner's case that said land was not subjected to any acquisition for any national highway project in the past and despite which Respondent No.4 had threatened to take over the Petitioner's land for the purpose of national highway.
It is in these circumstances the present Petition came to be filed praying for the reliefs as noted by us hereinabove.
5. We have heard learned counsel for the parties on the earlier occasion and more particularly, on 30 th August, 2024, when we had passed the following order :
"1. Learned counsel for the parties have argued on a copy of the document which is dated 6 December, 2018 annexed at Exhibit 'I' (Page 109).

In paragraph 2 of this document, which is a communication from the Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition No.19), Pune to the petitioner wherein, it is stated that in 1966, the subject land was acquired for the purpose of National Highway No.50 (Khed-Sinnar Section), and that, copy of the award is also available.
In this regard, whether the same land is now being again subjected to acquisition, is the issue which is being raised which needs to be clarified by the National Highways Authority.
04 October, 2024.

sentences.text: We accordingly direct the Deputy Collector ( Land Acquisition No.19), Pune to place on record the award in regard to the statement as made in paragraph 2 of the letter dated 6th December, 2018.
Let this be undertaken on or before the adjourned date of hearing.
Let such record be placed on record on an affidavit or alternatively clarify paragraph No.2 of the said letter on an affidavit.

3. Stand over to 13 September, 2024.
4.

Ad-interim order, if any, shall continue to operate till the adjourned date of hearing."
6.

In the light of the aforesaid order, the Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition No.19),
Pune-Revannath Baburao Labade has placed on record their reply affidavit dated 30th September,
2024, wherein he has stated that in so far as letter dated 6 th December, 2018 as referred by us in our earlier order was concerned, the statement in such letter was made pursuant to the meeting held with the National Highway Authority on 27th November, 2018.

He has stated that to check the correctness of the statement made in the said letter, he had addressed a letter to the National Highway Authority on 6 th September, 2024 as well as to the other offices of the Land Acquisition Officers on 18 th September, 2024.

He stated that also his office called for a report from 04 October,
2024.
Priya Soparkar 39 wp 4742-22-c.doc
the other Land Acquisition Officers in respect of the award passed by any other Land Acquisition Officers in respect of village Chakan in respect of the land of the Petitioner.
He has placed on record the copies of such letters.

On receipt of the information as received by him in response to such letters, he has stated that after receipt of the report from all the Land Acquisition Officers and the National Highway Authority, it is seen that the Deputy Collector of Land (Land Acquisition No.19) had declared only two awards in the year 1966 for the purpose of diversion of Pune-Nasik Road bearing No.SR-21/66 and SR 26/66 and in the said award the Petitioner's land was not included in the said area.
7. Learned counsel for Respondent No.4 also does not dispute as to what has been stated in the affidavit as filed by the Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition No.19).
We note the relevant contents of the affidavit of the said, which reads thus :

"3. I say that, as per letter dated 06.12.2018, in para no.2, it was stated that the Award is made in the year 1966, for Village Chakan, Tal. Khed for State Highway No.50, and the copy of the Award is available in the office Respondent No.2.
I say that the said Statement is made pursuant to the meeting held with National Highway Authority on 27.11.2018.
I further say that, to check the correctness of this sentence made in the letter dated 06.12.2018, I have written a letter to National Highway Authority on 06.09.2024 as well as 04 October, 2024.
Priya Soparkar 39 wp 4742-22-c.doc
other offices of Land Acquisition Officers on 11.09.2024.

sentences.text: Acquisition Officers in respect of the Award passed by any other Land Acquisition Officer in respect of the village Chakan, in respect of the land of the Petitioner.

Hereto annexed and marked as Exhibit R1(Colly.) is a copy of the letter dated 06.09.2024, issued to National Highway Authorities and copies of the letters dated 11.09.2024 issued to other Land Acquisition Officers.

4. I say that, after receipt of the report from all the Land Acquisition Officers &
National Highway Authorities.

I say and submit that, my office has earlier declared only two awards in year 1966 for purpose of diversion of Pune-Nashik, bearing Nos.
SR 21/66 and 26/66 and in the said Award, the Gat No., of the Petitioner's land was not included in the said area.
5. In view of the abovementioned facts and circumstances, the Hon'ble Court may be pleased to pass an appropriate Order in the interest of justice."

8. In this view of the matter, the position on record is clear that the Petitioner's land in question was not acquired by publishing any award as per law and in the absence of such acquisition, it would not be valid for the Respondent No.4 to take away the Petitioner's land except by following due process of law that is subjecting the Petitioner's land in question to acquisition as per the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
04 October, 2024.
Priya Soparkar 39 wp 4742-22-c.doc 9.
In this view of the matter, we are of the clear opinion that the Petitioner will be entitled to the reliefs as prayed for.

10. We accordingly allow this Petition in terms of prayer clauses (b) and (c).
11.
Rule is made absolute and the Petition is allowed in the aforesaid terms.
No costs.
[ SOMASEKHAR SUNDARESAN, J. ] [ G. S. KULKARNI, J. ] 04 October, 2024.
